Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and honorable members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation. I am Joe Martin and I proudly represent the citizens of
Senate District 19, which includes much of Northern Oxford County and communities in
Franklin County. I am here today to present LD 2181, "Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in
Roxbury the Roxbury-Frye Veterans Memorial Bridge."
I urge the committee to support renaming the Frye Bridge, which is located on the Frye Crossover Road in Roxbury and goes over the Swift River, in honor of our veterans. I was
compelled to submit this bill after being contacted by several local veterans who requested
the change.
I believe such a designation would serve as a lasting tribute to the men and women who have
served our country with courage and sacrifice. This proposal has gained the support of the Roxbury Select Board and people in the community.
A bridge named for veterans would stand as a daily reminder of their dedication, resilience,
and the freedoms they helped secure for our community. It would also offer a meaningful way to express our collective gratitude, not just in words, but in a permanent and visible
way.
Americans owe an incredible debt to the men and women in uniform. This is the least we can do. I urge the committee to vote "ought to pass" on LD 2181. Thank you for your time
and thoughtful consideration of this proposal.

Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132"" Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither for Nor Against LD 2181
Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Roxbury the Roxbury-Frye Veterans Memorial
Bridge `

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at
MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 2181.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for this bridge. MaineDOT's
current inventory number for this structure is 2300.
Thank you.
